# Model card: Eczema likelihood (SCIN)

`cvm_eczema_likelihood_scin` v2 · module `eczema_photo` · target `eczema_likelihood` (probability) · status **needs validation** · trained 2026-10-17 by Training kit

## Intended use

Supporting signal in atopic dermatitis studies: flags captures that look less like eczema (e.g. a different rash, or a photo of the wrong site) for clinician attention. It does not grade severity: SCIN has no EASI or SCORAD labels.

Every prediction goes to clinician review before it enters a participant's record. This model is not clinically validated and must not be used for diagnosis.

## Data

- **Dataset:** [SCIN: Skin Condition Image Network](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)
- **Licence:** SCIN Data Use License (attribution required; re-identification prohibited)
- **Citation:** Ward A, et al. Creating an Empirical Dermatology Dataset Through Crowdsourcing With Web Search Advertisements. JAMA Netw Open. 2024;7(11):e2446615.
- **Label:** `eczema` (expert), as `probability`
- **Captures used:** 5190 from 2730 cases/people; 1366 more failed the module's quality gate and were excluded
- **Notes:** Crowdsourced smartphone photos; dermatologist differential diagnoses; no severity grades.

## Performance (out-of-fold, grouped by case)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| MAE | 0.193 (predicting the mean: 0.199) |
| RMSE | 0.253 |
| Pearson r | 0.186 |
| AUC (label ≥ 0.5, 661 positives) | 0.639 |
| Folds / ridge λ | 5 / 30000 |

### By fitzpatrick

| Group | n | MAE | r | AUC | Excluded by quality gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FST1 | 554 | 0.174 | 0.199 | 0.657 | 190 (26%) |
| FST2 | 1806 | 0.186 | 0.211 | 0.653 | 458 (20%) |
| FST3 | 1453 | 0.200 | 0.161 | 0.626 | 395 (21%) |
| FST4 | 781 | 0.199 | 0.242 | 0.679 | 167 (18%) |
| FST5 | 413 | 0.204 | 0.155 | 0.625 | 104 (20%) |
| FST6 | 51 | 0.203 | -0.026 | 0.337 | 17 (25%) |
| unknown | 132 | 0.192 | -0.048 | 0.406 | 35 (21%) |

Worst subgroup (n ≥ 20): **FST6**, AUC 0.337.

## Limitations

- Trained on crowdsourced smartphone photos of many conditions; eczema is one label among ~400.
- Labels are dermatologists' differential diagnoses from photos alone, without examination or history.
- Inputs are a general-purpose ImageNet embedding plus colour and texture features from a rule-based skin mask; neither was designed for skin, so check the subgroup table.
- Not a severity score. A severity model needs clinician-graded photos (see training/DATASETS.md).

## Reproduce

```bash
python -m vfcv.run studies/eczema_likelihood_scin/study.yaml
```

Inputs: the 1040 features of `eczema_photo` plus embedding. Training kit v0.1.0.

# Model card: Rough or flaky skin (SCIN, self-reported)

`cvm_scaling_scin` v2 · module `eczema_photo` · target `scaling_likelihood` (probability) · status **needs validation** · trained 2026-10-17 by Training kit

## Intended use

Exploratory proxy for scaling in psoriasis and eczema studies, where the workflow builder marks scaling as "needs a new model". It shows how far the existing features get before a dedicated scaling model is trained on clinician-graded photos.

Every prediction goes to clinician review before it enters a participant's record. This model is not clinically validated and must not be used for diagnosis.

## Data

- **Dataset:** [SCIN: Skin Condition Image Network](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)
- **Licence:** SCIN Data Use License (attribution required; re-identification prohibited)
- **Citation:** Ward A, et al. Creating an Empirical Dermatology Dataset Through Crowdsourcing With Web Search Advertisements. JAMA Netw Open. 2024;7(11):e2446615.
- **Label:** `rough_or_flaky` (self report), as `binary`
- **Captures used:** 4396 from 2254 cases/people; 1121 more failed the module's quality gate and were excluded
- **Notes:** Crowdsourced smartphone photos; dermatologist differential diagnoses; no severity grades.

## Performance (out-of-fold, grouped by case)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| MAE | 0.390 (predicting the mean: 0.397) |
| RMSE | 0.442 |
| Pearson r | 0.133 |
| AUC (label ≥ 0.5, 1200 positives) | 0.584 |
| Folds / ridge λ | 5 / 30000 |

### By fitzpatrick

| Group | n | MAE | r | AUC | Excluded by quality gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FST1 | 467 | 0.390 | 0.097 | 0.568 | 153 (25%) |
| FST2 | 1579 | 0.382 | 0.092 | 0.560 | 398 (20%) |
| FST3 | 1228 | 0.384 | 0.140 | 0.583 | 323 (21%) |
| FST4 | 651 | 0.395 | 0.086 | 0.558 | 136 (17%) |
| FST5 | 337 | 0.418 | 0.259 | 0.658 | 80 (19%) |
| FST6 | 38 | 0.393 | 0.072 | 0.540 | 16 (30%) |
| unknown | 96 | 0.466 | 0.351 | 0.698 | 15 (14%) |

Worst subgroup (n ≥ 20): **FST6**, AUC 0.540.

## Limitations

- The label is the contributor's own description, not a clinician's assessment of scale.
- Only cases where the contributor described the texture are used.
- Scale is a fine texture; the module's single texture feature (Laplacian variance) also responds to blur and camera noise.

## Reproduce

```bash
python -m vfcv.run studies/scaling_scin/study.yaml
```

# Model card: Finger-tapping score, MDS-UPDRS 3.4 style (synthetic)

`cvm_tapping_updrs_synthetic` v1 · module `finger_tapping` · target `tapping_score` (0-4) · status **needs validation** · trained 2026-10-17 by Training kit

## Intended use

Demonstrates the end-to-end path for a movement-disorder study model. Replace the dataset with clinician-rated videos (e.g. TULIP) before using the score for anything.

Every prediction goes to clinician review before it enters a participant's record. This model is not clinically validated and must not be used for diagnosis.

## Data

- **Dataset:** Synthetic finger-tapping tracks (rule-labelled)
- **Licence:** Generated in this repository (MIT)
- **Label:** `updrs_3_4` (synthetic), as `score`
- **Captures used:** 800 from 800 cases/people; 0 more failed the module's quality gate and were excluded
- **Notes:** Labels apply the MDS-UPDRS 3.4 anchor wording to known ground truth with assumed numeric cut-offs; not clinician ratings.

## Performance (out-of-fold, grouped by case)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| MAE | 0.570 (predicting the mean: 0.774) |
| RMSE | 0.742 |
| Pearson r | 0.631 |
| Folds / ridge λ | 5 / 100 |

### By fps

| Group | n | MAE | r | AUC | Excluded by quality gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24 | 266 | 0.556 | 0.699 | – | 0 (0%) |
| 30 | 254 | 0.533 | 0.608 | – | 0 (0%) |
| 60 | 280 | 0.617 | 0.596 | – | 0 (0%) |

Worst subgroup (n ≥ 20): **60**, MAE 0.617.

## Limitations

- Labels come from rules applied to synthetic ground truth, with assumed numeric cut-offs for slight/mild/moderate slowing. They are not clinician ratings.
- Synthetic tracks start after landmark detection; detection on real video is tested separately (services/cv/tests/test_video_e2e.py).
- A linear head cannot reproduce the scale's max-of-domains rule exactly; errors cluster at score boundaries.

## Reproduce

```bash
python -m vfcv.run studies/tapping_updrs_synthetic/study.yaml
```

Inputs: the 10 features of `finger_tapping`. Training kit v0.1.0.

# Model card: Rest tremor amplitude score, MDS-UPDRS 3.17 style (synthetic)

`cvm_tremor_updrs_synthetic` v1 · module `hand_tremor` · target `rest_tremor_score` (0-4) · status **needs validation** · trained 2026-10-17 by Training kit

## Intended use

Demonstrates the path for a tremor study model. The amplitude bands are defined in cm; converting from hand-size units assumes a 10 cm hand, so the score needs calibration on clinician-rated videos before use.

Every prediction goes to clinician review before it enters a participant's record. This model is not clinically validated and must not be used for diagnosis.

## Data

- **Dataset:** Synthetic hand-tremor tracks (rule-labelled)
- **Licence:** Generated in this repository (MIT)
- **Label:** `updrs_3_17` (synthetic), as `score`
- **Captures used:** 800 from 800 cases/people; 0 more failed the module's quality gate and were excluded
- **Notes:** Labels apply the MDS-UPDRS 3.17 amplitude bands to known ground truth, assuming a 10 cm hand; not clinician ratings.

## Performance (out-of-fold, grouped by case)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| MAE | 0.294 (predicting the mean: 0.822) |
| RMSE | 0.387 |
| Pearson r | 0.914 |
| Folds / ridge λ | 5 / 0.01 |

### By fps

| Group | n | MAE | r | AUC | Excluded by quality gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24 | 248 | 0.308 | 0.914 | – | 0 (0%) |
| 30 | 258 | 0.280 | 0.916 | – | 0 (0%) |
| 60 | 294 | 0.292 | 0.915 | – | 0 (0%) |

Worst subgroup (n ≥ 20): **24**, MAE 0.308.

## Limitations

- Labels come from rules applied to synthetic ground truth, assuming a 10 cm wrist-to-knuckle hand. They are not clinician ratings.
- Synthetic tracks start after landmark detection; detection on real video is tested separately (services/cv/tests/test_tremor_video_e2e.py).
- Camera shake from a hand-held phone looks like hand tremor; the protocol asks for a propped-up phone.
- The 0-4 bands are log-spaced in amplitude; a linear head on linear amplitude fits them only approximately.

## Reproduce

```bash
python -m vfcv.run studies/tremor_updrs_synthetic/study.yaml
```

Inputs: the 8 features of `hand_tremor`. Training kit v0.1.0.
